title: Struct Members and Member Access
learningObjectives: Access struct members using the dot operator.
Use arrow operator when accessing through a pointer.
Read and update member values correctly.
Use members in expressions and conditions.
Distinguish object access from pointer access.

understand.concept: Members are fields or functions belonging to a type. The dot operator accesses a member through an object; arrow accesses a member through a pointer to an object.
understand.whyItMatters: Member access keeps related data and operations grouped.
understand.explain: Use dot for objects and -> for object pointers; ensure member names and types match.

examples.title: Dot operator
examples.explanation: Dot accesses a member through an object.

examples.title: Arrow through pointer
examples.explanation: Arrow is member access through a pointer.

examples.title: Change multiple fields
examples.explanation: Each field can be assigned independently.

examples.title: Member in condition
examples.explanation: A field can participate in a decision.

practise.guidedTask: For Struct Members and Member Access, trace every example. List each type, object, member, initial value, access path, and state change. Identify where encapsulation or initialization affects correctness.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ model focused on Struct Members and Member Access (such as a Point, Student, Product, or Account). Include multiple objects, initialization, at least one operation/member access, and test normal, boundary and invalid states. Explain which fields should be public or private and why.
hints: Define the type and its responsibilities before creating objects.
Initialize members deliberately and trace their values.
Use dot for objects and arrow only for pointers.
Keep fields private when they must enforce rules.
Test object creation, valid operations and rejected updates.

questions.explanation: Arrow accesses members through a pointer.
Access names must refer to declared members.

questions.explanation: Fields can be part of expressions.
